abstract: Data-driven technologies have revolutionized indus-trial monitoring systems, such as liquid-level detection. However, restricted access operations and potentially explosive environments pose significant challenges in developing reliable monitoring solutions. Advanced data-driven methods are utilized instead of traditional techniques to address these issues through nondestructive testing. An experimental study was conducted using ultrasound propagation within a confined area. The goal is to comprehend the intricate wave behavior when waves encounter the free surface (water-air interface) between two ultrasonic transducers positioned and operating in through-transmission mode.

articleTitle: Suppression of Side Lobe Using Spectral Weights of Channel Data in Medical Ultrasonic Imaging System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE UFFC Latin America Ultrasonics Symposium (LAUS)
abstract: In the receive focusing in an ultrasound imaging system, we calculate the magnitude of the main and side lobe spectrum of received channel data using a two-dimensional Fourier transform. During the ultrasound receive focusing process, if signals coming from outside the imaging point are not completely removed, side lobe occurs in the image. Because the time signal of the side lobe is difficult to distinguish from the time signal of the imaging point, it is hard to remove it using time domain filter processing. However, if the received channel-time data is transformed by a two-dimensional Fourier transform, the spectrum of the main lobe and side lobe can be separated in the spectral domain. Therefore, the magnitude of the main lobe and side lobe spectra and the distance between the centroid of the two spectra were used to design a time domain side lobe suppression filter weight. We suppress the side lobe by multiplying the ultrasound image by spectral weights. To assess the filter performance, ultrasound RF data from the human organs were synthesized on a computer at the 5 MHz and 64-channel linear array transducer. We compared the conventional focusing image, weights applied image, Hamming apodization image, and the main lobe only image. Computer simulations showed a significant increase in the contrast of the lesion while maintaining resolution.

articleTitle: Immunoagglutination Diagnosis with Acoustofluidic Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE UFFC Latin America Ultrasonics Symposium (LAUS)
abstract: Immunoagglutination assays rely on the detection of the chemical interaction between antibodies (Ab) and antigens (Ag), which occurs through non-covalent bonds. Agglutination refers to the formation of macroscopic aggregates of nanoparticles. In this method, the antigen or antibody is immobilized on the surface of inert particles. Our goal is to introduce an acoustofluidic chip that catalyzes the Ag-Ab reaction. Acoustofluidic technology utilizes ultrasonic forces within microfluidic systems. Here, we present the results of the acoustofluidic-enhanced agglutination test to detect C-reactive protein (CRP) and antibodies against streptolysin O toxin (ASO). Our findings demonstrate an eight-fold increase compared to conventional tests.

articleTitle: Background-Free Detection of Light-Activatable Perfluorocarbon Nanodroplets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE UFFC Latin America Ultrasonics Symposium (LAUS)
abstract: Perfluorocarbon nanodroplets (PFCnDs) have been studied as an activatable ultrasound contrast agent. During vaporization, light-activatable PFCnDs generate characteristic ultrasound and photoacoustic (US/PA) signals across a sequence of images. As more PFCnDs vaporize in a region of interest, the US contrast increases exponentially while PA contrast decreases similarly. Previous studies have explored background-free imaging algorithms to show the location of the activated PFCnDs, by detecting the slope of exponential signals. In this study, we generate background-free images by identifying exponential trends and signal amplitudes, thus giving the location of PFCnDs and scaling the images by approximate PFCnD concentration. Synthetic US/PA images were generated by simulating a time-series of US/PA images during PFCnD activation events. Tissue background signals (offset) and random noise were also included. The algorithm analyzes intensity values to detect exponential trends using the coefficient of determination <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}})$</tex>, followed by image reconstruction. A pixel-wise pre-filtering was performed to account for offset and noise. Then, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}}$</tex> coefficient was calculated to evaluate how each pixel's data fit an exponential behavior. Image reconstruction used the parameters of the fitting function generated, using the estimated amplitude value to scale the concentration image. A Pearson correlation coefficient was used to assess the accuracy of the algorithm by comparing the reconstructed image with the ground truth image. The algorithm was tested under presence of up to 70% noise and 50% signal offsets to assess the potential applicability in realistic tissue environments. In these conditions, the algorithm showed strong performance with high correlation coefficients. The successful reconstruction of background-free images suggests the feasibility of this method for further testing in vivo.

articleTitle: Segmentation of Ultrasound Images for the Detection of Breast Nodules
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE UFFC Latin America Ultrasonics Symposium (LAUS)
abstract: The importance of early detection of breast abnormalities, with a special focus on nodules, has been demonstrated in order to effectively combat breast cancer, one of the main causes of global mortality. The implementation of a collaborative system, working as an aid to diagnosis through ultrasound examinations, aims to improve the effectiveness of diagnosis, allowing early treatment and reducing adverse events. The system uses techniques from binarization, processing, including a filter to minimize speckle noise and improve image sharpness, and calculations, in order to obtain effective identification. In segmentation, after obtaining a binary image, it is subdivided into meaningful regions for detailed analysis and understanding of the scene. In order to identify the nodule effectively and safely. The implementation of this system could contribute to early treatment, avoiding adverse events, as well as improving the chances of a cure and reducing the need for unnecessary invasive procedures.
